answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond and books one timber load at an island mill, where an auditor seals it to its key and logs the seal in the kernel ledger. The queue fee rises: the k-th load pays 20+3(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th fake pays 3,017, and 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 in bonds plus 1,518,500 in fees, because a seal cannot be reused. An honest agent locks 80 once, pays 20, and recovers it after a clean epoch. A seal-rental ring fails: a rented seal carries the wrong key, so the auditor burns the bond, voids the load, and a raven reports the void to the kernel ledger.
